subject: Logging & exportability: retention windows and audit trail export questions

Subject: Questions on logging retention/exportability for RFP

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the RFP template — a few follow-ups from our security/compliance team as we prepare scoring: we want clear, scorable answers for the audit log and exportability section. Can you confirm the following for Redwood hosted (SaaS) and Dedicated (reserved) deployments? Please be as specific as possible.

1) Retention windows: what are default retention periods for audit logs and request logs (in days)? Are there hard maximums? Can customers configure retention per-tenant?
2) Exportability: do you provide bulk export tools for raw audit logs? Supported formats (JSONL, Parquet, CSV)? Is export incremental or snapshot-based?
3) Evidence & chain-of-custody: do exported logs include signed timestamps / tamper-evidence? Is there a recommended way to produce forensics packages for audits?
4) Deletion/ERAS request handling: if a customer requests deletion of records, how is that recorded and how are exports affected?
5) Hosted vs Private differences: any differences in retention/export features for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments?
6) PII & redaction: any built-in masking or redaction at export time?

We’d appreciate a short matrix and any sample export commands or links to a runbook.

Regards,
Danielle Park
Security Operations Manager
Aurelius Health

--

Hi Danielle —

Thanks — great, specific questions. I’m looping in Rishi (Applied ML / infra security) and Laura from legal for the parts about deletion/chain-of-custody. I’ve attached a short matrix that answers the first-pass items and a sample export command. Below are quick bullets; Rishi and Laura will add technical/legal precision. If helpful we can also share a short recorded demo of a bulk export job.

Quick summary (high-level):
- Retention defaults: Hosted: 90 days request logs, 365 days audit trails (configurable up to 2 years under contract). Dedicated: default 365 days for both; can be extended via reserved config. Private: fully configurable by customer (subject to their infra).
- Exports: Bulk exports supported via secure S3 presigned URLs or direct streamed export to customer S3. Formats: JSONL (primary), Parquet (for analytics), CSV for light exports. Exports support incremental snapshots (daily delta) and full snapshots.
- Tamper evidence: Exported objects include signed manifest with SHA256 checksums and export metadata (start/end timestamps, export job id). For highest integrity we recommend exporting to a WORM-enabled S3 bucket.
- Deletion handling: All deletion requests are logged in the audit trail (event type: data_deletion_request). Deletion operations are reversible only via retention policy exceptions and are recorded in export manifests.
- Redaction: We support configurable redaction rules at export time (PII masks, field-level hashing).

I’ve attached: redwood_log_archival_matrix.pdf (matrix), export_instructions_sample_commands.txt (example aws s3 cp / signed-url examples).

Thanks Marissa — adding technical details for the RFP scoring table.

Hi Danielle — I’ll keep this concise and scorable.

- Hosted (SaaS):
  * Audit logs: default retention 365 days (configurable in 30-day increments up to 730 days under Enterprise contract).
  * Request/trace logs: default 90 days (max 365 days).
  * Snapshot/export cadence: full export snapshots available on-demand; incremental (delta) exports can be scheduled daily. Exports include a manifest.json with job_id, utc_start, utc_end, file_list, sha256sums.
  * Format: primary JSONL (line-delimited JSON), optional Parquet for analytic pipelines. CSV available for user-facing fields only.
  * Integrity: export tool signs manifest with Hermetic job key; manifests are versioned and stored alongside exported objects. We provide an export verification script that checks checksums and manifest signatures.

- Dedicated: same capabilities as Hosted, with two differences: 1) retention caps are set by the customer's committed configuration and 2) we can run on-site export agents that stream raw logs directly to the customer's S3 (no intermediate persistence in our shared object store).

- Private (VPC / on-prem): fully customer-controlled. Our private control plane provides the same manifest/format, but you control retention, WORM, KMS keys (BYOK / HSM).

- Deletion / ERAS (GDPR style) handling: deletion requests generate an immutable audit event and a deletion manifest entry that is included in subsequent exports. When an object is physically removed from a hosted store (per policy), exports will reference the deletion manifest entry and a redaction marker instead of the removed payload. Documented process: 1) submit request via portal or SOC ticket, 2) legal review (if required), 3) deletion job with export manifest entry, 4) confirmation to customer. Laura — happy to capture the legal wording for the RFP.

- Forensics / chain-of-custody suggestions: export to WORM bucket, enable server-side KMS with an HSM-backed key, sign manifests using our job signing key, and attach the job signature to the audit ticket. We can also produce a zip package with (manifest.json, indices.parquet, checksums.sha256, job_signing_certificate.pem) on request.

If you want, we can run these commands against a small dev export and share artifacts for your auditor to validate.

-Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Danielle — attaching the consolidated matrix and a short runbook excerpt with sample commands. Quick practical notes you can include in scoring: 

- Export options: 1) On-demand full export (single snapshot), 2) Scheduled incremental exports (daily delta), 3) Streaming export agent for Dedicated/Private that sends log lines in near real-time to customer S3.
- Formats: JSONL is the canonical export format (schema v1.4). Parquet is available as a post-process conversion for analytics.
- Sample validation command (attached file has full text):
  aws s3 cp \"https://s3-presigned.example.com/export-2026-07-19.tar.gz\" ./ && sha256sum export-2026-07-19.tar.gz && python verify_manifest.py manifest.json --verify-signature job_signing_certificate.pem
- PII redaction: configurable pipeline stage that can run at export time (pre-export) or at ingestion time (mask before persistence). For auditable exports we include a redaction_summary.json in the package describing rules applied.

Attachments: redwood_log_archival_matrix.pdf, export_instructions_sample_commands.txt, SOC2-summary-2025.pdf

Would you like a short recorded walkthrough or a live call this week to see an export job run end-to-end? We can provision a one-off dev export for your auditors.

Best,
Marissa
